messages:
Laura: Heads up — saw a sharp p99 jump on /v1/generate right after we shifted fallback weight to eu. p50/p95 look unchanged. Dashboard: https://redwood.dev/d/latency?panel=tail :eyes:
Amir: Looking now. Was that the policy flip at 10:42 UTC?
Sasha: Yep, that was me. I bumped eu-fallback from 0.05 -> 0.17 to absorb the overflow. Here's the change I pushed:
```
route_weights:
  global: 0.83
  eu-fallback: 0.17
```
Tyler: Are we sure the console rollup is isolating region-level histograms? If it's merging then different KV cache hit distributions could skew p99.
Laura: I checked infra metrics — kv_cache_miss for eu hosts jumped around the same time. Query I ran:
`sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (route,region)`
Amir: That suggests eu has both higher miss rate and longer tail. But the magnitude of p99 change looks too big for just cache misses; could be sample-merging artifact when route weights move.
Sasha: Dashboard shows "composite sampling enabled" on that rollup. If the global p99 is a blend of a high-volume low-latency population and a low-volume high-tail population, changing weights can move the estimator.
Marcus: Quick hypothesis: when sample_count for global rollup drops or gets re-tagged, tdigest/rollup interpolation can step. I see sample_count halved right after the flip.
Tyler: Can we repro with a controlled split? I can spin a canary that routes 15% to eu and send steady traffic for 30m.
Laura: Yes please. Also capture raw histograms per-region (not just tdigest). If we can get the two raw distributions we can compute exact combined percentiles and rule out estimator bugs.
Amir: Also double-check we didn't accidentally change model_variant on eu nodes (quantized vs fp16) — different decode latencies can amplify tail.
Sasha: Confirmed model variant same. But eu infra is on driver 1.8 vs 2.0 in us-west. Opening infra ticket to reconcile drivers.
Marcus: Action items: annotate the dashboard with the policy flip, run per-region raw-histogram export, run the 15% canary test, and if reproduced add a temporary alert for >2x p99-on-change during rollout. :+1:
Laura: I'll run the exports and post the artifacts here. Thanks — keeping this short: major theory = mixing populations + sample-count drop. Will follow up with numbers.
Deploy Bot: Deployment sasha/route-weight-change succeeded at 2025-06-07T10:42:15Z
Laura: Ack, noted. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
